metadata.title: ICT QUESTIONNAIRE FOR PISA 2022 (International Option) Main Survey Version

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is a PISA 2022 ICT questionnaire instrument (International Option) rather than an empirical analysis paper. It specifies item content and response scales for students’ reported access/use of digital resources, but it does not describe sampling, complex survey design, or any estimation procedure that would require student or replicate weights. Therefore, no weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) can be extracted from the provided text. For any downstream empirical use of PISA 2022 ICT questionnaire responses, analysts should apply the official PISA sampling weights and replicate design as provided in the PISA technical documentation for the corresponding dataset release.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values handling is not applicable because this is an assessment questionnaire specification document, not an analysis of cognitive achievement scores that would use PVs. The text provided contains item wording and response options only, with no modeling of PV-based outcomes and no description of an estimation pipeline. Missing-data handling is not reported because the document does not present any statistical analysis or imputation/deletion strategy for questionnaire responses.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the full available sample for the specified countries.

data.outcome_summary: This document provides the PISA 2022 International Option ICT questionnaire items (Main Survey Version) that collect students’ self-reported access to and use of digital resources at school and outside school, perceptions of resource availability/quality, and frequency of digital activities across learning and leisure contexts. It includes multiple item blocks (e.g., device/internet access frequency, agreement with statements about availability and technical support, classroom subject-specific ICT use, and activities such as creating presentations, searching online, and receiving feedback). The response formats are ordinal categories (e.g., never/almost never to several times a day; strongly disagree to strongly agree; and time-use bands). No sampling design, scaling model, plausible values, or statistical results are included in the provided text, so the instrument’s role is to define measurement rather than to report empirical predictive performance or benchmarks.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction is sparse because the provided content is an instrument/questionnaire specification rather than an empirical study with an analytic sample, model training, or reported outcomes. As a result, fields such as total_students, country-level sample sizes, ML techniques, and main findings cannot be populated from the text shown. This is consistent with a methodology/instrument document that defines item content and response scales without conducting statistical analysis.
